inputs.name: U whole diploid genome, amino-acid class
inputs.cite: Keightley 2012 Abstract as quoted in H7 formal statement; H7 q1

inputs.name: mu, new mutations per diploid genome

day.reading: the sqrt(N) trick helps with mutational load, not the speed of adaptation (H4 q3); the deleterious side is separate from Haldane's cost of beneficial fixation
day.holds: the record's numbers are all on the deleterious side; Keightley states the paper does not address beneficial substitutions or Haldane 1957

critic.reading: U = 2.2 is too high for hard selection but tolerable under relative-fitness selection or synergistic epistasis (H7 q1); no detectable fitness decline is expected (H7 q2)
critic.holds: W = 0.11 needs 17.8 selective deaths per 20 offspring (1/W = 9.0), which is the 'one mutation, one death' arithmetic Keightley rejects as a description of human selection

notes: All printed figures reproduce: e^-2.2 = 0.1108 (0.11), e^-0.35 = 0.7047 (0.7), 20 x (1 - 0.1108) = 17.8 (18). The 70 new mutations per diploid genome at mu = 1.1e-8 imply about 3.2e9 sites per haploid genome. No raw Keightley text is in sources/raw/ in this checkout; the inputs are the Abstract as quoted in H7 and quotes-literature. parameters mutation.new_mutations_per_genome.common_citation is [60, 100], not the 70 the H7 link line attributes to it (70 is inside the range). The sqrt(N) purge has no held number.
